proposes_relationship_type.name: THEMATICALLY_RESEMBLES
proposes_relationship_type.definition: THEMATICALLY_RESEMBLES(a,b) asserts: these two passages make comparable statements about a shared referent, on evidence that is not their shared wording. Symmetric, emitted once in ascending canonical_key order. It is NOT NORMALIZED_EQUIVALENCE, NOT CANONICAL_IDENTITY, NOT a TEXTUAL_VARIANT and NOT a near duplicate: no normalisation of any kind establishes an edge here, and every pair reachable by an existing textual predicate, by USES_FORMULA co-membership, by identical folded Sanskrit surface, by agent 12's staged relations, or at a lexical char-4gram cosine of 0.20 or above is refused by construction.
proposes_relationship_type.note: not in src/vedagraph/enrich/predicates.py CONTROLLED_PREDICATES and not one of the 14 frozen semantic predicates. Proposed for addition, not assumed. It does not collide with ADDRESSES_CONCERN or CONCERNS (passage-to-Concept) nor with the 5 predicates refused by name in vedagraph.semantic.ontology. It is not a generic RELATED_TO: it means one thing and is refused wherever it cannot be defended.

defects_found: MY OWN, and it decided the tier structure: the referent guard read corpus-level devata_attr, which merges HAS_DEVATA (RV, 210 English display labels) and HAS_DEVATA_ASCRIPTION (AV, 324 Sanskrit ascription forms). The two vocabularies intersect in 0 values, so a set intersection across them can never be non-empty and the guard was refusing every RV-AV pair for a vocabulary reason dressed as an evidential one. Found because TIER_A came back with zero cross-Veda edges, which is not a plausible fact about the Vedas.

INHERITED, and every per-pair number depended on it: pool_scores.npz was aligned to a pool 199 pairs shorter than the one on disk, because the previous run rebuilt its corpus and embeddings and never re-ran the pair scorer. Up to 1,037,092 of 1,133,112 positions were attached to the wrong pair. The aggregate threshold table barely moved, so plausibility could not have caught it; a length check did.

MY OWN TOOLING: np.load on an .npz is lazy, so Z[name] re-decompresses the whole 1.13-million-element array from the zip on every access. A per-edge access pattern did that 215,030 times and burned 913 seconds of CPU with no output. Materialising the arrays once made the same work instant.

MY OWN SURFACE, reproducing agent 10 independently: 873 of 1,975 Yajurvedic verses (44.2%) carry a Vedic sign that survives my accent fold with no counterpart on the transliterated RV/AV side -- 780 with U+1CEA + U+1CED and 141 with U+0901 candrabindu, and 3 SV verses, and 0 in RV and AV. This biases the lexical control on those verses. Excluding every Yajurvedic endpoint RAISES the leakage AUC to 0.8447, so no conclusion here depends on it.
